evidence.quote: In my view, there is no need to be in a hurry to make further policy rate adjustments.
If the labor market were to weaken unexpectedly or inflation were to fall more quickly than anticipated, policy could be eased accordingly.
While inflation is well down from its recent peak, the latest data have largely shown it moving sideways.
Growth has remained solid so far but has started to show some signs of slowing.
If uncertainty persists or worsens, economic activity may be constrained.
The current policy stance is well positioned to deal with the risks and uncertainties that we face in pursuing both sides of our dual mandate.

parsed.rationale: The speaker favors holding a moderately restrictive rate with no hurry to cut, noting stalled inflation progress and tariff-driven inflation expectations. She balances this against signs of slowing growth and possible labor softening, with easing contingent on data, yielding a roughly neutral, slightly hawkish-leaning stance.
